impact:
The maintainer's genuine Codex session ID (verified present at ~/.codex/sessions/2026/07/09/) is hard-coded in a src/codex.ts:30 comment, survives tsc into dist/codex.js:28 (no removeComments), and dist/ is in package.json "files" — so it ships in every npm tarball once T-007 publishes. usage.py:199 carries the same literal but stays out of the tarball; it remains exposed via the public repo. Bare identifier only, no conversation content.

TRIAGE ADDITION (2026-07-31): a second identifier of the same class ships too — src/context.ts:141-142 carries USER=<real-account> and /Users/testuser/.codex in a comment that compiles into dist/context.js:80-81 (verified in the current build). The packaging contract test catches neither, because its attribution grep reads only package.json, never tarball file contents. T-007's gate: scrub BOTH sites and extend the contract grep to unpacked tarball contents.
resolution:
Scrubbed both shipping sites and closed the blind spot that let them through.

FIXED (both compiled into dist/, which is in package.json "files"):
- src/codex.ts:30 — the real rollout ID `rollout-2026-07-09T00-43-18-019f45d4-...` replaced with the fixture convention `rollout-2026-01-01T10-00-00-<session id removed — T-024>` (UUIDv7 shape, random bits zeroed). Comment now states why a real name must not appear there and points at the new guard.
- src/context.ts:141-142 — `USER=<real-account>` / `/Users/testuser/.codex` replaced with `testuser`, the synthetic account the test suite already uses. The worked example's pedagogical content is unchanged.
- dist/codex.js and dist/context.js verified clean after rebuild.

NOT FIXED, deliberately (both are T-007 openQuestion 3, an owner decision, and neither ships in the tarball):
- usage.py:199 carries the same literal but is the frozen oracle; modifying it needs an explicit exemption plus a parity re-run.
- product-architecture-2026-07-30.md:10 carries a home path + Claude session UUID. Repo-side residue only.
- LICENSE's "Copyright (c) 2026 Amir Shayegh" ships, but the MIT copyright holder is T-007 openQuestion 1 — not an autonomous call.

DURABLE FIX — tests-ts/contract/packaging.contract.mjs now unpacks the tarball and scans shipped file CONTENTS, not just package.json. The old attribution test read only JSON.stringify(MANIFEST), which is why 16 green contract tests missed both identifiers. Three new assertions:
1. "carries no personal name outside the LICENSE copyright line" — /<maintainer-name>/i over all shipped content; the single exemption is narrow (LICENSE Copyright lines only), so the name appearing anywhere else in LICENSE still fails.
2. "carries no real session identifier" — any UUID in shipped content must end `-7000-8000-0000000000xx` (version/variant nibbles plus zeroed random bits). Real UUIDv7 random bits cannot match; this is exactly the example-vs-real-session distinction.
3. "carries no real home directory path" — /Users/<x> and /home/<x> must name a placeholder (testuser, you, user, me).

MUTATION-VERIFIED, all three (green tests alone would prove nothing here):
- Reintroducing the real rollout ID → assertion 2 fails ("non-synthetic UUID in shipped content").
- Reintroducing the username + home path → assertions 1 and 3 both fail.
- Adding the name to LICENSE off a Copyright line → assertion 1 fails, confirming the exemption is not a blanket file skip.

Suite after fix: 314 unit tests pass, contract 19/19 (was 16), parity --final 266 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped, 45/45 goldens byte-match, `npm run test:all` exit 0.
